newsitem.title: USA: Marvel widens losses for quarter, year.
newsitem.headline: Marvel widens losses for quarter, year.

text.p: Marvel Entertainment Inc., involved in a tempestuous battle with financier Carl Icahn, Friday reported a greater loss for the fourth quarter and full year.
The comic book and trading card company had a fourth quarter loss of $436.5 million, or $4.29 a share, compared with a year earlier loss of $58.5 million, or 58 cents a share.
Revenues fell to $164.3 million from $2.32.8 million a year earlier.
For the year, Marvel lost $464.4 million, or $4.56 a share, on revenues of $745.5 million. In 1995, Marvel lost $48.4 million, or 48 cents a share, on revenues of $828.9 million.
Earlier this week, Carl Icahn lost a round in court in his fight for Marvel when a federal judge blocked a group led by the financier from taking control of the comic book publisher.

A U.S. Bankruptcy Court judge granted a temporary restraining order Monday that prevents a bondholder group led by Icahn from taking control of the board of directors of Marvel, said officials representing bondholders and Marvel.
"Today's court ruling means that Marvel and the banks are free to explore all options to protect the company's future," said a Marvel spokesman. He declined further comment.
Bondholders had planned to replace Marvel's current board with their own slate of directors, after foreclosing on 80 million Marvel shares that was collateral for the bonds.

The ruling was just the latest in a battle between Icahn and Ronald Perelman, who bought Marvel in 1988 when it was a relatively small comic book publisher. He expanded it with the purchase of Fleer and SkyBox International trading card companies.
